en: Thus spoke the Lord, the Holy Buddha: "This great instruction is most difficult to attain; it is the essence of all mantras. The Lord Buddha exists within the Great Dissolution (mahāpralaya); from that, he emerges. He is the progenitor of the Lord Pañcatathāgata, distinguished by his body and names. What is the nature of his form? His mudrā is Bodhyagrī; his wisdom is Śāśvata; his wheel is Sañjata. His title is Sahavati; his lion-throne is Atutuṅgaṅa. He is Bharālī Satvavajrī, he is Bharālī Dharmavajrī, and he is Bharālī Karmavajrī. Together with the goddess Amarivṛtta, she is situated above his body, at the very center of the navel, serving as his abode."

Lord Akṣobhya resides in the east; his color is black. His consort is the goddess Locanā. His mantra is *Hūṃ*. His mudrā is Bhūsparśa. His wisdom is Ādarśana-jñāna (Mirror-like Wisdom). His vajra is Sañjata. His celestial realm is called Abhirati. His mount is a tall elephant. He is known as Lord Vajrarāja, Lord Vajrarāga, Hyang Vajrasādhu, and Lord Vajradharādi. He is the one who turns the wheel of immortality (*amarivṛtta*). He resides within the body; his dwelling place is in the center of the joints.

Lord Ratnasambhava resides in the south; his color is yellow. His consort is the goddess Māmakī; her mantra is *traṃ*, her wisdom is *ākāśamati*, her skull-cup is formed from the *sañjata* [mudrā], and the center of the *limpa* is her abode.

The Lord Amitābha resides in the west; his color is red. His consort is the goddess Pāṇḍaravāsinī. His mantra is *Hrīḥ*. His wisdom is that of discernment (*pratavekṣaṇa-jñāna*). His mudrā is the meditation (*dhyāna*) mudrā. His attribute is a noose of serpents (*nāgapāśa*). His celestial realm is Sukhāvatī. His attendants are Lord Vajradharma, Lord Vajratīkṣṇa, Lord Vajraketu, and Lord Vajrabhāsa. They reside within his body, situated in the center of the heart as their dwelling place.

Lord Amoghasiddhi resides in the north; his color is variegated (*viśvavarṇa*). His consort is the goddess Bharaṇī Tārā; his mantra is *oṃ āḥ*; his mudrā is the *abhaya* (fear-dispelling) gesture; his gnosis is that of the "Accomplishment of Action" (*kṛtānuṣṭhāna-jñāna*). His celestial palace is named Kusumita; his mount is a lofty Garuḍa. Lord Vajrakarma, Lord Vajrarakṣa, [Lord Vajrayakṣa,] and Lord Vajrasandhi are his retinue. Indeed, he dwells within the body of the *jro hampū*, which serves as his abode.

Indeed, O Lord Pañcatathāgata, you have returned to these world-realms; you reside within our very bodies. You are the creator of the five wisdoms (*pañcajñāna*). As for what is called the five wisdoms, they are: the eye (*cakṣuh*), the ear (*śrotra*), the nose (*ghrāṇa*), the tongue (*jihvā*), and the heart (*hṛdaya*). The eye is the organ of sight; the ear is the organ of hearing; the nose is the organ of smell; the tongue is the organ of taste; and the heart is the organ of thought. These are what are termed the five sense-faculties (*pañcendriya*). Furthermore, as for the deities of the five sense-faculties: Lord Akṣobhya resides in the eyes; Lord Ratnasambhava resides in the ears; Lord Amitābha resides in the nose; and Lord Amoghasiddhi resides in the tongue. He is the one who provides the sense of taste for Lord Vairocana, who resides in the body as a whole. He is that which is eaten and consumed; therein, his *Sahadevī* (consort) is present at every moment. This is what is called the "Noble One of Fivefold Self" (*saṅ hyaṅ pañcātma*), who serves as the inner essence.
